source.quote: Bluesound's own product page for the NODE, read 2026-11-24: « HDMI eARC, optical, and analog audio inputs » against « RCA, optical, coaxial, and USB audio outputs ». Specifications: « 192 kHz », « Signal-to-Noise Ratio -118 dB », « Bit Depth 16-24 », « Distortion THD+N, 0.0007% », « DSD Support DSD256 », « Supported High-Quality Audio File Formats FLAC, MQA, WAV, AIFF, MPEG-4 SLS ». Also « THX AAA™ headphone amplifier technology with full-sized 1/4" headphone output ».

_the_page_that_separates_what_others_mix: Bluesound is the first maker in this pass to state inputs and outputs in two distinct sentences - « HDMI eARC, optical, and analog audio inputs » and « RCA, optical, coaxial, and USB audio outputs ». Eversolo, FiiO and Weiss each left me working out which was which, and the FiiO SR11 was nearly recorded with its outputs as inputs. Worth noting as a quality of a source, not just of a device.
_why_no_per_input_rates: « 192 kHz » and « Bit Depth 16-24 » are listed as general specifications, not against a named input, so they are recorded at DEVICE level only. Splitting them down onto the eARC and optical inputs would be an inference, and an unlikely one: optical is rated 96 kHz by four other makers in this catalogue. The inputs are named by the maker and rated by nobody - the same gap as fiio/k7, eversolo/dac-z10 and smsl/d200, now on its fourth record.
_no_chip: No converter is named. « THX AAA™ headphone amplifier technology » is the headphone stage, not the conversion stage, and recording it as the chip would confuse an amplifier with a converter - the distinction fiio/k7's three named parts made concrete.
